fixes.explanation: That's the reason the text gives. Elihu burned with anger against Job "…for justifying himself rather than God…" (Job 32:2). Elihu is Barachel's son, a Buzite, and he had been waiting to speak to Job (Job 32:4). Now the waiting is over.

That's not the reason the text gives. It says Elihu burned with anger because Job was "…justifying himself rather than God…" (Job 32:2). Advice never comes up in that verse. That's the whole story on his anger.

Yes, baker. Elihu's anger doesn't stop at Job. He also "…burned with anger against Job’s three friends because they had failed to refute Job, and yet had condemned him." (Job 32:3). Elihu is handing out anger like free cookie samples, one for Job and one for each friend.

That's it. "…Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he." (Job 32:4). He waited, and when he saw the three men had no further reply, his anger was kindled (Job 32:5). That's a lot of patience for one man.

The text never says anything about money. It says Elihu waited "…because the others were older than he." (Job 32:4). Age was the reason, not a bank account. Nobody was checking wallets to see who got to talk first.

Elihu doesn't bring up power at all. He says, "It is not only the old who are wise…" (Job 32:9). The group he names is the old, and his point is that wisdom isn't only theirs. A fancy title doesn't make this list. Years are the only thing on the table.

That's not what the text says. Elihu's plan is about whose arguments he'll use: "…I will not answer him with your arguments." (Job 32:14). As for waiting, he says, "…I waited while you spoke…" (Job 32:11), and later, "I too will answer…" (Job 32:17). So his point is about which arguments he'll use, not about Job speaking again.

Not quite, baker. Elihu says, "I will be partial to no one, nor will I flatter any man." (Job 32:21). He's saying he won't be partial and he won't flatter. That's quite a promise for a man this fired up.
